title: Inverse image of a torsion etale sheaf is torsion
statement: Let $u:U\to V$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and let $F\in\Ab(V_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] be a torsion abelian sheaf [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf]. Then its inverse image $u^{-1}F\in\Ab(U_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] is a torsion abelian sheaf.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, Section label section-torsion, Tag 0DDB (torsion sheaves), with Lemma label lemma-stalk-pullback, Tag 03Q1 ($(u^{-1}F)_{\bar x}=F_{u(\bar x)}$): the stalks of $u^{-1}F$ are stalks of $F$, hence torsion; equivalently $u^{-1}$ is exact and commutes with colimits, so $u^{-1}(F[n])=(u^{-1}F)[n]$ and $u^{-1}\varinjlim_nF[n]=\varinjlim_n u^{-1}F[n]$. Stacks states no separate lemma; the place is where the fact is used without comment

proof.text: Setting and additivity. Let $F\in\Ab(V_{\Et})$ be torsion [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf]. By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact] the functor $u^{-1}:\Ab(V_{\Et})\to\Ab(U_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] is exact, in particular additive: $u^{-1}(f+g)=u^{-1}f+u^{-1}g$ for parallel morphisms of abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], and $u^{-1}(1_F)=1_{u^{-1}F}$. Writing $n\cdot1_F=1_F+\dots+1_F$ ($n$ terms), induction on $n\ge1$ gives $u^{-1}(n\cdot1_F)=n\cdot1_{u^{-1}F}$: multiplication by $n$ is carried to multiplication by $n$.

source.place: Section 'Torsion sheaves' (label section-torsion, Tag 0DDB, line 13888; proof of Lemma 0DDC: F = union of the F[d]) and Lemma 03Q1 (label lemma-stalk-pullback, line 4649), part (1): f^{-1} on abelian sheaves is exact

proof.text: $n$-torsion subsheaves are preserved. For $n\ge1$ let $j_n:F[n]\to F$ be the kernel of $n\cdot1_F$ [def-pur-abelian-sheaf-kernel], and $j'_n:(u^{-1}F)[n]\to u^{-1}F$ the kernel of $n\cdot1_{u^{-1}F}$. By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact] $u^{-1}$ preserves kernels, so $u^{-1}(j_n):u^{-1}(F[n])\to u^{-1}F$ is a kernel of $u^{-1}(n\cdot1_F)=n\cdot1_{u^{-1}F}$ (step 1). Two kernels of the same morphism are uniquely isomorphic over the source: there is a unique isomorphism $\theta_n:u^{-1}(F[n])\xrightarrow{\sim}(u^{-1}F)[n]$ with $j'_n\circ\theta_n=u^{-1}(j_n)$. That is, $u^{-1}(F[n])=(u^{-1}F)[n]$ as subobjects of $u^{-1}F$.

source.place: Section 'Torsion sheaves' (label section-torsion, Tag 0DDB, line 13888; proof of Lemma 0DDC: F = union of the F[d]) and Lemma 03Q1 (label lemma-stalk-pullback, line 4649), part (1): f^{-1} on abelian sheaves is exact

proof.text: Compatibility with the transition maps. For $n\mid m$ let $t_{nm}:F[n]\to F[m]$ and $t'_{nm}:(u^{-1}F)[n]\to(u^{-1}F)[m]$ be the inclusions of the diagrams of [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf], so $j_mt_{nm}=j_n$ and $j'_mt'_{nm}=j'_n$. Then $j'_m\theta_m u^{-1}(t_{nm})=u^{-1}(j_mt_{nm})=u^{-1}(j_n)=j'_n\theta_n=j'_mt'_{nm}\theta_n$, and $j'_m$ is a monomorphism (a kernel), so $\theta_m\circ u^{-1}(t_{nm})=t'_{nm}\circ\theta_n$. Hence $\theta=(\theta_n)_n$ is an isomorphism from the diagram $n\mapsto u^{-1}(F[n])$ (the image under $u^{-1}$ of the diagram $n\mapsto F[n]$, indexed by the positive integers ordered by divisibility) to the diagram $n\mapsto(u^{-1}F)[n]$, and its inverse $(\theta_n^{-1})_n$ is again compatible with the transition maps; and $\theta$ carries the family $(u^{-1}j_n)_n$ to the family $(j'_n)_n$ of maps to $u^{-1}F$.

source.place: Section 'Torsion sheaves' (label section-torsion, Tag 0DDB, line 13888; proof of Lemma 0DDC: F = union of the F[d]) and Lemma 03Q1 (label lemma-stalk-pullback, line 4649), part (1): f^{-1} on abelian sheaves is exact

proof.text: Colimits. Let $(L,(\iota_n)_n)$ be the chosen colimit of $n\mapsto F[n]$ in $\Ab(V_{\Et})$ and $c_F:L\to F$ the canonical map, $c_F\iota_n=j_n$; let $(L',(\iota'_n)_n)$ be the chosen colimit of $n\mapsto(u^{-1}F)[n]$ in $\Ab(U_{\Et})$ and $c_{u^{-1}F}:L'\to u^{-1}F$ the canonical map, $c_{u^{-1}F}\iota'_n=j'_n$ [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf], [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. By [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-preserves-colimits] the cocone $(u^{-1}L,(u^{-1}\iota_n)_n)$ is a colimit of $n\mapsto u^{-1}(F[n])$ (the canonical map from the chosen colimit to it is an isomorphism). By step 3, $(\iota'_n\theta_n)_n$ is a cocone on $n\mapsto u^{-1}(F[n])$ and $(u^{-1}(\iota_n)\theta_n^{-1})_n$ a cocone on $n\mapsto(u^{-1}F)[n]$; the universal properties give $\alpha:u^{-1}L\to L'$ with $\alpha\,u^{-1}(\iota_n)=\iota'_n\theta_n$ and $\beta:L'\to u^{-1}L$ with $\beta\iota'_n=u^{-1}(\iota_n)\theta_n^{-1}$, and $\beta\alpha$, $\alpha\beta$ agree with the identities on all coprojections, hence are the identities by uniqueness: $\alpha$ is an isomorphism. Finally $c_{u^{-1}F}\,\alpha\,u^{-1}(\iota_n)=c_{u^{-1}F}\iota'_n\theta_n=j'_n\theta_n=u^{-1}(j_n)=u^{-1}(c_F\iota_n)=u^{-1}(c_F)\,u^{-1}(\iota_n)$ for all $n$ (step 2), so by uniqueness in the colimit $(u^{-1}L,(u^{-1}\iota_n))$, $c_{u^{-1}F}\circ\alpha=u^{-1}(c_F)$: under $u^{-1}(\varinjlim_nF[n])\cong\varinjlim_n(u^{-1}F)[n]$ the canonical map of $u^{-1}F$ is $u^{-1}$ of the canonical map of $F$.

source.place: Lemma 0038 (lemma-adjoint-exact, line 3472), part (1): left adjoints commute with colimits; used for f^{-1} in etale-cohomology.tex proof of Lemma 0A4B (line 18389)

proof.text: Conclusion. $F$ is torsion, so $c_F$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf]; a functor carries isomorphisms to isomorphisms, so $u^{-1}(c_F)$ is one, and $c_{u^{-1}F}=u^{-1}(c_F)\circ\alpha^{-1}$ (step 4) is an isomorphism. By [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf], $u^{-1}F$ is torsion.

split_report.summary: Statement kept (checked against def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf: torsion = canonical map colim_n F[n] -> F is an isomorphism). Stacks (etale-cohomology 0DDB, 03Q1) uses the fact without a lemma, so the proof is written by the agent from the colimit definition in five steps: u^{-1} additive, so u^{-1}(n)=n; u^{-1} preserves kernels, giving isomorphisms u^{-1}(F[n]) = (u^{-1}F)[n] over u^{-1}F; these are compatible with the divisibility transition maps; u^{-1} preserves colimits, so u^{-1}(colim F[n]) = colim (u^{-1}F)[n] and the canonical map of u^{-1}F corresponds to u^{-1}(c_F); hence it is an isomorphism.
